thread:
maya: paging — getting alerts for cross-region request failures from eu-west -> us-east, increased 5xx and 504s, customers reporting timeouts. looks like region pinning is sending traffic to wrong cluster.
oncall-bot: @maya was paged for incident INC-2026-489
maya: i'm taking it. ~ we're seeing spike at 11:12 UTC
eli: saw the same in grafana, compared steering decisions — cluster selection logs show fallback to older region config
dan: noticed a config push 10:58 that touched geo-routing policy, rolling back now
maya: can you run `redwoodctl route show --policy geo-steer --since 10m` and paste output?
dan: here's diff from 10:58
```
- match: latency <= 120ms -> region=eu-west
+ match: latency <= 120ms -> region=us-east
```
maya: that explains it — policy changed target region by mistake. but why did it hit only some AZs?
eli: looks like pinning metadata for certain customer sessions still targeted eu-west. when policy flipped, steering picked us-east for new sessions and left pinned sessions in eu-west, causing split routing and backend capacity imbalance -> errors
support-lead: customer impact: 12% of production requests for EU customers returned 502/504, several enterprise customers reported app errors
maya: mitigation plan: 1) revert policy change (dan) 2) run pin-sync job to re-evaluate pinned sessions (eli) 3) throttle new cross-region fallbacks for 15m (maya) 4) status page update (support-lead)
dan: rollback applied at 11:19 UTC — verifying metrics
oncall-bot: deploy rollback started by dan at 11:19:12 UTC — job id dep-2860012401
eli: running pin-sync now, command:
```
python tools/pin_sync.py --filter region=eu-west --dry-run=false --batch-size=500
```
eli: started at 11:21, ETA ~6m
maya: traffic already dropping toward normal on steering dashboard, 5xx rate reduced from 12% -> 4% at 11:24
support-lead: drafting status update: "We detected a routing policy configuration change that temporarily caused increased errors for requests originating from EU regions. The configuration has been reverted and we are actively reconciling session pinning. Some customers may see brief errors; continuing monitoring." Will publish in 10m unless rollback fully resolves.
pagerduty: esk check-in reminder scheduled in 15m
dan: one backend in eu-west shows container crashloop during overload, scaling up a hot pool and draining failing node
maya: please patch healthchecks for that node to avoid noisy evictions — filed infra task INFRA-734
eli: pin-sync finished at 11:28, reconciled 98% of session pins, 2% required manual follow-up
maya: metrics now at 0.7% 5xx for EU at 11:30 UTC — still watching for tail errors
support-lead: status posted to status.redwood.com at 11:31 UTC: "Investigating - Customers in EU may experience increased error rates due to a region routing policy change. Mitigation in progress."
maya: next steps: run a full correlation to customers with long-lived sessions and notify their CSMs if needed (support-lead)
support-lead: coordinating CSM outreach list, will send priority customers note in 20m
maya: assigning postmortem owner @eli — please include timeline, root cause (misapplied policy change), why pin-sync didn't auto-reconcile, and what safeguards to add (policy gating, CR review, automated pin-reconcile on policy change)
eli: ack — will start draft after incident closes
oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-489 status -> mitigated at 11:36 UTC
maya: closing thread, will monitor for 1hr then handoff to daily oncall
support-lead: thanks all :tada:
